From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@talentco.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final-round: noise reconciliation & tiebreak path for Z. Brooks

Team —

Quick snapshot: we have 5 total panel votes for Zane (attached scorecards). Raw numeric spread is tightly clustered: 3 reviewers at 7/10, 2 reviewers at 5/10 — majority leans hire but there is noise in system design assessment (two reviewers interpreted the rubric differently). Before I lock anything in GH, I want a concise convergence so recruiting has a clean adjudication.

Ask: please reply-all with a one-line final position by EOD PST (Hire / No Hire / Needs a short follow-up) and add any 1–2 sentence clarifying rationale for your vote if you changed it after revisiting the rubric. If you prefer, mark your final cell in the attached Zane_Brooks_scorecard.xlsx (tab: FINAL).

Notes & suggested tiebreak policy (if we stay split):
- If votes remain 3/2, default to majority.
- If we end 2/2 with one abstain, schedule a 15m tie-break with either Hiring Manager or Senior Eng (Jonas volunteered earlier).

Attachments: Zane_Brooks_scorecard.xlsx (panel scores), panel-synthesis-notes.txt (my quick read).

I pulled together short evidence bullets below for quick review (copied from synth notes):
- Product sense: solid (clear tradeoffs, prioritized metrics).
- System design: divergent — some flagged missing KV cache discussion, others satisfied with cache-first approach.
- Culture / collaboration: unanimous positive; clear ownership examples.

Thanks — brief replies appreciated. I can pulse a follow-up if we're still split at EOD.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Hiring Coordinator, Redwood Inference

Final: Hire.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Final-round: noise reconciliation & tiebreak path for Z. Brooks

Quick note — I stayed No Hire.

Why: two of the system-design prompts asked for explicit reasoning about KV cache eviction and long-tail latency mitigation; Zane glossed over eviction policies and the consequences for cold-start throughput. That gap matters for the infra work he'd own; product sense is good, but I don't think the systems readiness bar is met yet.

I'm open to a 10–15m sync if others feel strongly counter to that. If we do a quick call, I'd bring a short checklist of must-have system answers (eviction strategy, cache warmup, and a simple SLO/playbook).

—Aditya

Subject: Re: Final-round: noise reconciliation & tiebreak path for Z. Brooks

Thanks all for the quick replies — appreciate the crisp rationales. Summary / final decision:

- Votes: Marissa = Hire, Jonas = Hire (see note), Karthik = Hire (confirmed verbally), Aditya = No Hire, Tessa (coordinator read-in) = Hire. Final tally 4/1 in favor.
- Action: I'll mark GH as Advance to Offer and push to recruiting with the panel notes + the two flagged follow-up bullet points for the hiring manager to cover during onboarding (fast-track a short technical ramp plan addressing cache eviction clarity). Priya — can you open the req and start offer paperwork?

If anyone still has a hard objection, flag it before I lock the decision at 10:00 AM PST — otherwise I'll update Greenhouse and drop the synthesis doc in the candidate folder.

Evidence summary for hiring packet (1–2 lines each):
- Product/PM alignment: clear prioritization and metric thinking.
- Systems readiness: borderline but acceptable with a 30-day ramp plan and paired engineering shadowing.
- Collaboration & communication: strong (positive peer feedback).

Attachments for record: panel-synthesis-notes.txt (finalized), updated Zane_Brooks_scorecard.xlsx (FINAL tab). GH update: https://greenhouse.io/reqs/RED-4821 (attached to candidate record).

Thanks again — Tessa will drop the final note in the candidate folder.

—Tessa
